intro: AI tools for freelance translators on a Mac mostly help with the work around the translation: email, research, terminology checks and admin. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that sees your screen, points at things and answers out loud in any app. It does not operate other apps for you, so your CAT tool and your files stay in your hands.

Email, reply drafts, terminology lookups, Word review steps and reminders are where AI tools fit best on a Mac.

blocks.text: Where a translator's Mac day goes

Translators do not have a public time study that splits the week into translating, email and admin. That gap makes it hard to say which AI tool will pay off. The numbers below come from general office and knowledge workers. Read them as a warning sign, then time your own week before you buy anything.

Microsoft's 2023 Work Trend Index covered 31,000 full-time workers in 31 markets. For the average Microsoft 365 user, 57% of time goes to communication and 43% to creation. Email alone takes 15%. The heaviest 25% of email users spend 8.8 hours a week on it. Asana's Anatomy of Work Index, which surveyed over 10,000 knowledge workers, puts 60% of time into what it calls work about work. Asana's page does not give the study year, so use that figure with care.
CAT tools on Mac: what runs and what needs a virtual machine

Most freelance translators already use computer-assisted translation tools. A ProZ.com article based on more than 3,000 full-time professional translators reports that 88% use at least one CAT tool for at least some tasks. That article gives no survey year. Inbox Translation's 2023 survey had 2,803 respondents. Of those who answered, 81% use CAT tools at least some of the time, 59% use them often, and 19% never do.

The catch for Mac users is the tool itself. memoQ's Mac help page says memoQ doesn't have a Mac version. It has to run in a virtual Windows environment such as VMware Fusion, Parallels Desktop, Oracle VM or Boot Camp. Its system requirements page asks for at least 8 GB of RAM and recommends 16 GB or more. Budget for memory before you buy anything else.

blocks.title: Check the ARM line first
blocks.text: memoQ's requirements page says: We are not testing memoQ TMS on computers with ARM processors. Apple silicon Macs use ARM chips. The page names memoQ TMS, while the Mac page names the memoQ desktop app, so ask memoQ which product each statement covers before you commit.

blocks.text: Client email and reply drafts for translators

Client email is often where the time disappears, and it is the easiest place to get help. Many client messages come down to a deadline, a question about a term or a file. Hold ⌥ ⌘ while the message is open and ask what it needs from you. Lazur answers out loud, so your eyes can stay on the source text.

When you need a reply, ask for a draft, not a finished email. Give Lazur the facts you have already checked, such as the date and the glossary request. Then read every line. A draft that sounds right can still promise a date you never agreed to. Keep your own voice, and send the reply yourself.
Word and Google Docs review on Mac

Word for Mac is where many translators review, comment and hand off files. Microsoft's Office for Mac release notes list Version 16.114.3, Build 26102720, dated October 27, 2026. For Word and Outlook, those notes say only 'Quality and performance improvements.' To find your own build, open Word > About Word.

items: Find Review > Track Changes once, on a quiet day, so you know where it is before a deadline.

Ask Lazur to walk you through a PDF export, one click at a time, with the options you need.
Use ⌘F to find a term, then ask Lazur what the match means in the surrounding sentence.

blocks.text: If your client works in Google Docs, the same habits apply in Chrome. Lazur sees the page you have open and can explain a menu or a sharing setting in plain words. The Docs-specific steps are on [Google Docs for translators](/for/translators/google-docs).
Keep client material private before any AI tool sees it

This is the part most guides skip. Many client contracts and NDAs say what you may share, with whom, and where it can be stored. Read yours before you paste source text, a screenshot or a glossary into any AI tool. Some clients may forbid cloud tools outright. Others only want to know which tools you use.

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so Lazur can answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Those facts describe how Lazur handles data. They do not decide what your client allows, so close sensitive files before you hold the shortcut.

blocks.title: Your duties come first
blocks.text: This page does not claim any compliance certification for Lazur. Follow your client's rules and any NDA, even when a tool says it does not store content. For questions about your duties, ask your client or your professional association.
Admin, invoices and finding clients

Admin is hard to measure, and the public numbers are thin. Inbox Translation's 2023 survey found that 27% of respondents named knowing how to market themselves to ideal clients as a main challenge. It shows no time figures for invoicing or admin. On pay, the BLS reports a 2025 median of $60,170 a year for interpreters and translators in the US. It projects 2% growth from 2025 to 2035, which it calls slower than average.

Use Lazur for admin that has a clear next step. Ask it to set a reminder for an invoice check, or to draft a polite follow-up to a client who has not paid. Do not hand it your rates. Rates depend on your language pair, your niche and your costs, and only you can weigh those.

Mistakes translators make with AI tools

items: Pasting client text into a tool before reading the contract.
Trusting a draft reply without checking dates, names and figures against your notes.
Buying a tool for a task that takes only a few minutes a week.
Blaming the Mac when the real problem is a CAT tool's memory or its virtual machine settings.
Measuring nothing, then guessing which task to automate first.

blocks.title: Start with one task
blocks.text: Choose the task that wastes the most time you can name. For many people that is reply drafting or hunting through menus. Try one for a few weeks, then decide whether it earns a place in your day.
What to do next if you translate on a Mac

items: Read your client contracts for rules on tools, data and storage.
Keep a simple time log for a few weeks, with buckets for translating, email and admin.
Check the requirements for your CAT tool before you install a virtual machine.
Try one task with Lazur, such as a reply draft or a reminder.
Compare plans on the [pricing page](/pricing) once you know which task matters most.

blocks.text: When you are ready, [download Lazur](/download) for macOS. It runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. Lazur explains, points, guides, dictates and drafts. It does not click or edit for you, so your files and your judgment stay with you.

blocks.title: What this page cannot tell you
blocks.text: No translator-specific study in this research gives hours for email, admin or typing. The Inbox and ProZ surveys cover tool use only. ITI published a Translation Productivity report in June 2022, but this page does not use its findings.

faq.question: Is there an AI tool that translates for me on a Mac?
faq.answer: Lazur does not operate other apps for you. It sees your screen, explains what is on it, points at controls, guides you one click at a time, dictates and drafts text. Translation and final delivery stay your work. Check your client contract before any client text goes near an AI tool.

faq.question: Which CAT tools run on a Mac?
faq.answer: memoQ says it does not have a Mac version. Its Mac help page says it must run in a virtual Windows environment such as VMware Fusion, Parallels Desktop, Oracle VM or Boot Camp. Read the memoQ system requirements before you set up a virtual machine, because the page says it does not test on ARM processors. Lazur is not an add-in for any app, so it does not plug into memoQ.

faq.question: Does Trados Studio run on a Mac?
faq.answer: This page could not confirm the answer from RWS's own pages, so check the vendor's current documentation before you buy. Some community threads, several years old, describe running Windows software through Parallels or VMware. Those threads are not official guidance.

faq.question: Can Lazur help me in Word for Mac?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur sees the Word window, points at menu items such as Review > Track Changes, guides you one click at a time, and dictates text at the cursor when you hold fn. It does not click buttons or edit your document. More on Word is on [Word for translators](/for/translators/word).

faq.question: Does Lazur store or send my client's documents?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so Lazur can answer, and they are not stored. Content is not used to train AI models. Your client contract still decides what you may share, so check it before you hold the shortcut over sensitive material.

faq.question: How much time can AI save a freelance translator?
faq.answer: No translator-specific study in this research gives a reliable figure. General office data puts email at 15% of time for the average Microsoft 365 user. Track your own email and admin for a few weeks, then decide which task is worth handing to a tool.

faq.question: Do I need an Apple silicon Mac for Lazur?
faq.answer: Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Your CAT tool is a separate question. For memoQ, the requirements page asks for 64-bit Windows 10 or Windows 11 and 8 GB of RAM, with 16 GB or more recommended. Check that page before you choose a virtual machine setup.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Windows is planned, not available. Lazur runs on the Mac.

painPoints.text: General office data puts 15% of the average Microsoft 365 user's time into email. The heaviest 25% of email users spend 8.8 hours a week on it. These are not translator figures, so treat them as a warning sign.

painPoints.title: Work about work crowds out the translation

painPoints.text: 81% of Inbox Translation's 2023 respondents use CAT tools at least some of the time. memoQ's Mac help page says memoQ doesn't have a Mac version and must run in a virtual Windows environment.

painPoints.title: Finding clients takes its own time

painPoints.title: Software sits behind every step
painPoints.text: The BLS says nearly all translators use software in their work. It names computer-assisted translation tools that draw on a translation memory, and machine translation post-editing.
